content.intro: This lesson focuses on yaml formatting and linting and connects the PDF syllabus topics to a small, inspectable example. Work from the intended data model, write down the expected result, then verify syntax and semantics with the target tool.
content.why_it_matters: YAML Formatting and Linting matters because structured-data files sit between people, tools, services, and deployment systems. A clear contract and repeatable checks make the result easier to maintain and safer to consume.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A YAML parser processes text into a representation and then constructs language-specific values. Parser libraries differ in API, supported version/schema, and safety defaults, so use safe loading, explicit versions, and real-target tests.

content_blocks.title: What you will cover

Rule configuration.; Suppressing or resolving specific warnings. Integrating linting into continuous integration.. Treat each as part of a workflow: define what the data should mean, represent it consistently, and test how the chosen implementation interprets it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: YAML Formatting and Linting
content_blocks.code:
yamllint config.yaml
yq ".app.name" config.yaml

Install and pin the intended tool before using it in CI; verify which implementation of yq is installed.
content_blocks.expected_output: Linting and querying are different operations; tool names can refer to implementations with different syntax and behavior.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Indentation and scalar interpretation are part of the data model. Quote ambiguous strings, use consistent spaces, and test with the parser/schema that the target application actually uses. Confirm implementation-specific behavior against the target parser, tool version, and standards documentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating readable text as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Syntax and visual formatting cannot establish data types, schema conformance, or application-specific meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse, validate against the intended contract, and test a valid plus an invalid fixture.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every parser interprets the feature identically.
common_mistakes.why: Format versions, schema choices, library defaults, and product-specific restrictions affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the exact parser/version and test the target environment.

common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, wrong types, duplicate keys, or ambiguous scalars may still break consumers.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep valid, invalid, and boundary fixtures in version control.
